dedupe_keys.name: jena greyfield redevelopment inselplatz with climate sensitive urban planning and the jelka tool germany

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Jena, a city of about 108,000 people in the Saale valley in Thuringia, Germany, built heat adaptation into urban planning, using the redevelopment of the Inselplatz greyfield site for a university campus as its example. The city's adaptation strategy JenKAS rests on a handbook on climate-sensitive urban planning, with local climate conditions, legal aspects, economic assessments of options and good practice, and a decision support tool called JELKA for urban stakeholders. For Inselplatz, three design alternatives were compared on four criteria: investment and maintenance costs of paving, water features, lawns and trees and the net present value of green roofs at a 1.5% discount rate, modelled heat stress, architectural quality and amenity value. Planning ran from 2012 to 2017 and construction was to start in late 2020, with EU-funded buildings due by 2023. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal (2020), from the FP7 project BASE. Caveats: results are appraisals, not monitored outcomes, and the page predates completion. It illustrates multi-criteria and cost-benefit appraisal of green infrastructure against urban heat; a related record is i-Tree.
name: Jena greyfield redevelopment (Inselplatz) with climate-sensitive urban planning and the JELKA tool (Germany)
outcomes: Three redevelopment alternatives were compared on cost, heat stress, architectural quality and amenity, and adaptation was mainstreamed into Jena's planning with a permanent adaptation budget.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study on the City of Jena
resources_used: multi-criteria and cost-benefit comparison of three designs
